bookInfo.name: Old History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Xue Juzheng et al.

title.zh: 卷一百三十 周書21: 列傳十 王峻 慕容彥超 閻弘魯 崔周度
title.en: Volume 130 Book of Later Zhou 32: Biographies 10 - Wang Jun, Murong Yanchao, Yan Honglu, Cui Zhoudu
title.raw: 卷一百三十 周書21: 列傳十 王峻 慕容彥超 閻弘魯 崔周度 Volume 130 Book of Later Zhou 32: Biographies 10 - Wang Jun, Murong Yanchao, Yan Honglu, Cui Zhoudu

sentences.zh: 王峻，字秀峰，相州安陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jun, style name Xiufeng, was a native of Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, whose courtesy name was Xiufeng, came from Anyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父豐，本郡樂營使。

translations.literal: His father Feng served as director of the prefecture's music office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feng held the post of director of the prefectural music corps.

sentences.zh: 峻幼慧黠善歌，梁貞明初，張筠鎮相州，憐峻敏惠，遂畜之。

translations.literal: In childhood Jun was clever and sharp and skilled at song; in the early Zhenming era of Liang, Zhang Jun governed Xiang Prefecture, took pity on Jun's quick wit, and kept him in his household.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Wang Jun was bright, quick-witted, and gifted at singing. Early in the Liang reign era Zhenming, when Zhang Jun was posted as military governor of Xiang Prefecture, he took a liking to the boy's cleverness and kept him in his service.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗入魏州，筠棄鎮南渡，以峻自隨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Weizhou, Jun abandoned his post and crossed south, taking Jun with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong marched into Weizhou, Zhang Jun gave up his command and fled south across the river, bringing Wang Jun along.

sentences.zh: 時租庸使趙巖訪筠於其第，筠召峻聲歌以侑酒，巖悅，筠因以贈之，頗得親愛。

translations.literal: At the time Rent and Corvee Commissioner Zhao Yan called on Jun at his residence; Jun summoned Jun to sing aloud to accompany the wine; Yan was pleased, and Jun therefore presented him as a gift, and he won considerable affection.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Yan, commissioner for rent and corvée labor, visited Zhang Jun at his mansion. Jun had Wang Jun sing to enliven the drinking, and Yan was delighted. Jun then gave Wang Jun to him as a gift, and Yan came to treat him with real fondness.

sentences.zh: 梁亡，趙氏族滅，峻流落無依，寄食於符離陳氏之家，久之彌窘，乃事三司使張延朗，所給甚薄。

translations.literal: When Liang perished, the Zhao clan was exterminated; Jun drifted without support, lodged for food at the home of the Chen family in Fuli, and after long hardship grew still more destitute, then served Three Departments Commissioner Zhang Yanlang, whose stipend was very meager.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liang fell and the Zhao clan was wiped out, Wang Jun was left adrift with nowhere to turn. He lived on charity at a Chen household in Fuli; as months passed his plight grew worse, and he finally entered the service of Zhang Yanlang, commissioner of the Three Departments, who paid him very little.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，延朗誅，漢祖盡得延朗之資產仆從，而峻在籍中，從歷數鎮，常為典客。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai, Yanlang was executed; the Han founder took all of Yanlang's assets and attendants, and Jun was on the register; he followed through several postings and was regularly made reception officer.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Qingtai reign, Zhang Yanlang was put to death. The Han founder Liu Zhiyuan seized all of Yanlang's property and retainers; Wang Jun was listed among them. He served in one commandery after another, usually as master of ceremonies for visiting guests.

sentences.zh: 漢祖踐阼，授客省使，奉使荊南，留於襄、漢為監軍，入為內客省使。

translations.literal: When the Han founder ascended the throne, he was appointed envoy of the Guest Reception Bureau, sent on mission to Jingnan, left at Xiang and Han as supervisory commissioner, and entered the capital as commissioner of the Inner Guest Reception Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Zhiyuan took the throne, Wang Jun was made envoy of the Guest Reception Bureau, dispatched on embassy to Jingnan, then left behind as army supervisor at Xiangyang and Hanzhong, and later recalled to the capital as commissioner of the Inner Guest Reception Bureau.

sentences.zh: 及趙思綰作亂於永興，漢隱帝命郭從義討之，以峻為兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When Zhao Sizong rebelled at Yongxing, the Hidden Emperor of Han ordered Guo Congyi to suppress him and made Jun military superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Sizong rose in rebellion at Yongxing, Emperor Yin of Later Han ordered Guo Congyi to campaign against him and appointed Wang Jun superintendent of army and horse affairs.

sentences.zh: 從義與峻不協，甚如水火。

translations.literal: Congyi and Jun were not in accord, like fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Congyi and Wang Jun could not work together; their relations were as hostile as fire and water.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to commissioner of the Northern Court of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reassigned as commissioner of the Northern Court of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 賊平，加檢校太傅，轉南院使。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was given the additional title of Grand Preceptor on inspection and transferred to commissioner of the Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed he received the honorary title of Grand Preceptor and was moved to commissioner of the Southern Court.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮鄴，兼北面兵馬，峻為監軍，留駐鄴城。

translations.literal: When the Taizu held Ye, he also held northern frontier armies and horses; Jun was army supervisor and remained stationed at Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei was posted at Ye, he also commanded the northern frontier armies; Wang Jun served as army supervisor and stayed garrisoned in Ye.

sentences.zh: 隱帝蕭墻變起，峻亦為群小所構，舉家見害。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor's palace coup erupted, Jun was also framed by petty men, and his whole household was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Emperor's palace coup broke out, Wang Jun was likewise framed by petty schemers, and his entire family was slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 從太祖赴闕，綢繆帷幄，贊成大事，峻居首焉。

translations.literal: Following the Taizu to the capital, he planned closely in the command tent and helped accomplish the great enterprise; Jun stood foremost among them.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Guo Wei to the capital, he worked closely in the command tent and helped bring the great enterprise to success; Wang Jun ranked first among those who did so.

sentences.zh: 京師平定，受漢太后令，充樞密使。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, he received the command of the Han empress dowager and was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was secured, he received orders from the Han empress dowager and was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太祖北征，至澶州，為諸軍擁迫，峻與王殷在京聞變，乃遣侍衛馬軍都指揮使郭崇往宋州，前申州刺史馬鐸往許州，以防他變，二州安然，亦峻之謀也。

translations.literal: When the Taizu marched north and reached Cangzhou, pressed by the armies, Jun and Wang Yin in the capital heard of the change and then sent Palace Guard cavalry commander Guo Chong to Song Prefecture and former Shen Prefecture inspector Ma Duo to Xu Prefecture to guard against other disturbances; the two prefectures remained secure—this too was Jun's plan.
translations.idiomatic: On Guo Wei's northern campaign, when he reached Cangzhou and was pressed forward by his troops, Wang Jun and Wang Yin in the capital learned of the upheaval. They sent Palace Guard cavalry commander Guo Chong to Songzhou and former Shenzhou inspector Ma Duo to Xuzhou to forestall other trouble; both prefectures stayed calm—another stratagem of Wang Jun's.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，加平章事，尋兼右僕射、門下侍郎平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: When the Taizu ascended the throne, he was given the additional post of Grand Councilor; soon he also held Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Councilor and Gate Department Attendant, and supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei took the throne, Wang Jun was made Grand Councilor; soon afterward he also served as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Gate Department Attendant and Grand Councilor, and supervised compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷初建，四方多故，峻夙夜奉事，知無不為，每侍太祖商榷軍事，未嘗不移時而退，甚有裨益。

translations.literal: At the time the court was newly founded and the four quarters had many troubles; Jun served day and night, doing whatever he knew to do; whenever he attended the Taizu to discuss military affairs he never withdrew before an hour had passed, and he was of great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty was newly established and troubles pressed on every side. Wang Jun attended the emperor day and night, undertaking whatever task he could. Whenever he stood by Guo Wei to discuss military affairs he never left before an hour had passed, and his counsel proved highly useful.

sentences.zh: 然為性輕躁，舉措率易，以天下之事為己任，每有啟請，多自任情。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was light and rash, acting in a careless way, taking the affairs of the realm as his own charge; whenever he made a request he mostly followed his own whim.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was by nature impulsive and rash, acting with little deliberation, treating the affairs of the empire as his personal burden. When he petitioned the throne he usually did as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 太祖從而順之，則忻然而退；

translations.literal: When the Taizu followed and assented, he would withdraw in pleasure;
translations.idiomatic: If Guo Wei agreed, Wang Jun would withdraw in satisfaction;

sentences.zh: 稍未允可，則應聲而慍，不遜之語隨事輒發。

translations.literal: if assent was slightly withheld, he would grow angry on the spot, and disrespectful words would issue at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: but if the emperor hesitated even slightly, he would flare up at once, and impertinent words spilled out on every occasion.

sentences.zh: 太祖素知其為人，且以佐命之故，每優容之。

translations.literal: The Taizu had long known his character, and because he had helped establish the dynasty, he always treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei had long known what sort of man he was, and because Wang Jun had helped him seize the throne, he always indulged him.

sentences.zh: 峻年長於太祖二歲，太祖雖登大位，時以兄呼之，有時呼表字，不忘布衣之契也。

translations.literal: Jun was two years older than the Taizu; though the Taizu had ascended the throne, he sometimes addressed him as elder brother and sometimes called him by his courtesy name, not forgetting their bond as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was two years older than Guo Wei. Even after Guo Wei became emperor he would sometimes call him elder brother and sometimes use his courtesy name, never forgetting their friendship from humbler days.

sentences.zh: 峻以此益自負焉。

translations.literal: Jun for this reason grew still more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: This only made Wang Jun all the more conceited.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年冬，劉崇與契丹圍晉州，峻請行應援，太祖用為行營都部署，以徐州節度使王彥超為副。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Guangshun, Liu Chong and the Khitan besieged Jin Prefecture; Jun asked to go in relief; the Taizu employed him as supreme commander of the campaign army and made Xu Prefecture military governor Wang Yanchao his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the first Guangshun year, Liu Chong of Hedong and the Khitans besieged Jinzhou. Wang Jun volunteered to lead the relief force; Guo Wei appointed him supreme commander of the field army and named Xuzhou military governor Wang Yanchao his deputy.

sentences.zh: 詔諸軍並取峻節度，許峻以便宜從事，軍行資用仰給於官，隨行將吏得自選擇。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all armies to take Jun's command; Jun was permitted to act as circumstances required; campaign expenses were supplied by the state, and accompanying officers and clerks might be chosen by himself.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed every army under Wang Jun's command, allowed him discretionary authority on campaign, ordered that marching expenses be drawn from the treasury, and let him pick his own staff of officers and clerks.

sentences.zh: 將發之前，召宴於滋德殿，太祖出女樂以寵之。

translations.literal: Before setting out he was summoned to a feast in the Zide Hall, and the Taizu brought out female musicians to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he marched, Guo Wei feasted him in the Zide Hall and sent out palace musicians to show him special favor.

sentences.zh: 奉辭之日，恩賜優厚，不拘常制。

translations.literal: On the day of his farewell audience the gifts were generous beyond ordinary rule.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took leave, the rewards were lavish and broke with usual precedent.

sentences.zh: 及發，太祖幸西莊，親臨宴餞，別賜御馬玉帶，執手而別。

translations.literal: When he set out, the Taizu visited the Western Villa and personally attended the farewell feast, additionally bestowing an imperial horse and jade belt, and parted holding his hand.
translations.idiomatic: As he departed, Guo Wei went to the Western Villa to give him a personal farewell banquet, also granting an imperial horse and jade belt, and took his hand at parting.

sentences.zh: 峻至陜駐留數夕，劉崇攻晉州甚急，太祖憂其不可支，議親征，取澤州路入，與峻會合，先令諭峻。

translations.literal: Jun reached Shan and halted several nights; Liu Chong pressed the attack on Jin Prefecture very hard; the Taizu feared it could not hold and discussed a personal campaign, entering by the Ze Prefecture route to join Jun, first ordering that Jun be informed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun reached Shanzhou and lingered several nights. Liu Chong's assault on Jinzhou grew fierce; Guo Wei feared the city could not stand and debated leading the campaign in person, entering by way of Zezhou to join Wang Jun, and first sent orders to notify him.

sentences.zh: 峻遣驛騎馳奏，請車駕不行幸。

translations.literal: Jun sent a relay rider in haste to memorialize, asking that the imperial carriage not go on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun dispatched a courier at full gallop with a memorial asking that the emperor not take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 時已降御劄，行有日矣，會峻奏至，乃止。

translations.literal: At the time an imperial rescript had already been issued and the day of departure was fixed; when Jun's memorial arrived, the journey was halted.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial rescript had already gone out and the departure was set; but when Wang Jun's memorial arrived, the emperor stopped.

sentences.zh: 峻軍既過絳郡，距平陽一舍，賊軍燔營，狼狽而遁。

translations.literal: After Jun's army passed Jiang Prefecture, one stage from Pingyang, the rebel army burned its camp and fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Jun's army passed Jiangzhou, a day's march from Pingyang, the enemy burned their camp and fled in disarray.

sentences.zh: 峻入晉州，或請追賊，必有大利，峻猶豫久之，翌日方遣騎軍襲賊，信宿而還。

translations.literal: Jun entered Jin Prefecture; some urged pursuit of the enemy, saying there would surely be great gain; Jun hesitated long, and only the next day sent cavalry to strike the enemy, returning after two nights.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun entered Jinzhou. Some urged him to pursue the fleeing foe for a great prize; he hesitated a long while, and only on the morrow sent cavalry after them, returning two days later.

sentences.zh: 向使峻極力追躡，則並、汾之孽，無噍類矣。

translations.literal: Had Jun pursued with all his strength, the spawn of Bing and Fen would have left no mouth to feed.
translations.idiomatic: Had Wang Jun pressed the pursuit with all his might, the rebels of Bing and Fen would have been wiped out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 峻亦深恥無功，因計度增修平陽故城而回。

translations.literal: Jun also deeply shamed his lack of achievement and therefore planned and enlarged the old walls of Pingyang before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of accomplishing so little, Wang Jun spent his efforts enlarging the old walls of Pingyang, then marched back.

sentences.zh: 時永興軍節度使李洪信，漢室之密戚也，自太祖踐阼，恒有憂沮之意，而本城軍不滿千，峻出征至陜州，以救援晉州為辭，抽起數百人，及劉崇北遁，又遣禁兵千餘人，屯於京兆，洪信懼，遂請入朝。

translations.literal: At the time Yongxing military governor Li Hongxin was a close kinsman of the Han house; since the Taizu ascended the throne he had constantly been anxious and dejected, while the garrison of his seat numbered fewer than a thousand; when Jun marched out and reached Shan Prefecture, on the pretext of relieving Jin Prefecture he drafted several hundred men, and after Liu Chong fled north he also sent more than a thousand palace troops to garrison Jingzhao; Hongxin was afraid and therefore asked to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongxin, military governor of Yongxing, was a close relative of the Han imperial clan. Since Guo Wei took the throne he had been uneasy and downcast, and his capital garrison held fewer than a thousand men. When Wang Jun marched to Shanzhou on the pretext of relieving Jinzhou, he drafted several hundred troops from Hongxin's command; after Liu Chong retreated north he also stationed more than a thousand imperial guards at Chang'an. Terrified, Hongxin petitioned to come to court.

sentences.zh: 峻軍回，太祖厚加優賜。

translations.literal: When Jun's army returned, the Taizu heaped rewards upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun's army came back, Guo Wei showered him with favors.

sentences.zh: 時慕容彥超叛於兗州，已遣侍衛步軍都指揮使曹英、客省使向訓率兵攻之。

translations.literal: At the time Murong Yanchao rebelled at Yan Prefecture; the Palace Guard infantry commander Cao Ying and Guest Reception envoy Xiang Xun had already been sent with troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao had rebelled at Yanzhou. Palace Guard infantry commander Cao Ying and guest-reception envoy Xiang Xun were already leading troops against him.

sentences.zh: 峻意欲自將兵討賊，累言於太祖曰：「慕容劇賊，曹英不易與之敵耳。

translations.literal: Jun wished to command the troops himself to suppress the bandit and repeatedly told the Taizu, "Murong is a fierce bandit; Cao Ying is not easily his match."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun wanted to lead the campaign himself and told Guo Wei again and again, "Murong Yanchao is a ferocious rebel; Cao Ying will not easily stand against him."

sentences.zh: 」太祖默然。

translations.literal: The Taizu was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei said nothing.

sentences.zh: 未幾親征，命峻為隨駕一行都部署，破賊之日，峻督軍在城南，其眾先登，頗有得色。

translations.literal: Before long he campaigned in person and appointed Jun supreme commander of the accompanying column; on the day the bandit was broken, Jun directed the army on the south of the city; his troops were first to scale the wall and looked quite pleased with themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guo Wei took the field in person and named Wang Jun supreme commander of the accompanying column. On the day the city fell, Wang Jun directed the force south of the wall; his men were the first over the ramparts and wore a look of triumph.

sentences.zh: 從駕還京，未幾貢表乞解樞機，即時退歸私第。

translations.literal: Returning with the imperial progress to the capital, before long he submitted a memorial asking to be relieved of the Bureau of Military Affairs and at once retired to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the capital with the emperor, he soon submitted a memorial asking to leave the Bureau of Military Affairs and withdrew at once to his private house.

sentences.zh: 峻貪權利，多機數，好施小惠，喜人附己。

translations.literal: Jun was greedy for power and profit, full of schemes, fond of granting small favors, and pleased when others attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun craved power and profit, trafficked in intrigue, liked to hand out petty favors, and delighted in gathering followers.

sentences.zh: 太祖登極之初，務存謙抑，潛龍將佐未甚進用，其後鄭仁誨、李重進、向訓等稍遷要職，峻心忌之，至是求退，蓋偵太祖之意也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taizu's accession he strove to keep humility; the generals who had aided him before the throne were not much advanced, but afterward Zheng Renhui, Li Chongjin, Xiang Xun, and others were gradually moved to important posts; Jun envied them in his heart; by this time he sought to retire, essentially to probe the Taizu's mind.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei first took the throne he cultivated modesty and did not promote his old comrades from before the throne. Later Zheng Renhui, Li Chongjin, Xiang Xun, and others gradually rose to key posts. Wang Jun resented this. His request to retire was chiefly a probe of the emperor's intentions.

sentences.zh: 未陳請之前，多發外諸侯書以求保證，旬浹之內，諸道馳騎進納峻書，聞者驚駭其事。

translations.literal: Before stating his request he sent many letters to outer governors seeking pledges of support; within ten days and more couriers from every circuit galloped in presenting Jun's letters, and those who heard were shocked at the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Before he filed his petition he wrote widely to regional governors asking them to vouch for him. Within a fortnight couriers from every circuit raced in with Wang Jun's letters, and the court was alarmed by the spectacle.

sentences.zh: 峻連貢三章，中使宣諭無虛日，太祖嚴駕將幸其第，峻聞之，即馳馬入見，太祖慰勞久之，復令視事。

translations.literal: Jun submitted three memorials in succession; palace envoys came daily with imperial assurances; the Taizu was about to visit his residence in full state; when Jun heard of it he galloped in to audience; the Taizu comforted him at length and ordered him back to duty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun sent up three memorials in a row; imperial envoys came every day with reassuring words. Guo Wei was preparing to visit his house in full ceremonial array. Hearing this, Wang Jun rode at once to audience; the emperor comforted him at length and ordered him back to office.

sentences.zh: 峻又於本院之東，別建公署，廓廡廳事，高廣華侈。

translations.literal: Jun also built a separate official residence east of his bureau, with broad corridors and halls lofty, wide, and lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun also erected a new official compound east of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with broad corridors and reception halls tall, spacious, and sumptuous.

sentences.zh: 及土木之功畢，請太祖臨幸，恩賜甚厚。

translations.literal: When the earthworks were finished he asked the Taizu to visit in person, and the favors bestowed were very great.
translations.idiomatic: When construction was finished he invited Guo Wei to visit in person, and the gifts showered on him were lavish.

sentences.zh: 其後內園新起小殿，峻視之，奏曰：「宮室已多，何用於此？

translations.literal: Afterward a small hall was newly built in the inner park; when Jun saw it he memorialized, "The palaces are already many—what use is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Later a small hall was raised in the inner park. Wang Jun saw it and memorialized, "The palace already has more rooms than it needs—why build this?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「樞密院舍宇不少，公更自興造何也？

translations.literal: The Taizu said, "The Bureau of Military Affairs has no lack of buildings—why did you raise new ones yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei replied, "The Bureau of Military Affairs has plenty of offices—why did you put up still more for yourself?"

sentences.zh: 」峻慚默而退。

translations.literal: Jun withdrew in shame and silence.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun withdrew, abashed and speechless.

sentences.zh: 時峻以前事趙巖，頗承寵愛，至是欲希贈官立碑。

translations.literal: At the time Jun had formerly served Zhao Yan and enjoyed his favor; by now he wished to obtain posthumous honors and a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun had once served Zhao Yan, who had favored him; now he hoped to win posthumous honors and a memorial stele for Yan.

sentences.zh: 或謂峻曰：「趙巖以諂佞事君，破壞梁室，至今言者無不切齒，茍如所欲，必貽物議。

translations.literal: Someone told Jun, "Zhao Yan flattered and fawned upon his lord and ruined the Liang house; to this day those who speak of him gnash their teeth—if you get what you wish you will surely invite public censure."
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him, "Zhao Yan won favor through flattery and helped destroy the Liang dynasty. People still curse his name. If you have your way you will invite a storm of criticism."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: He therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 巖侄崇勛，居於陳郡，峻為求官田宅以賜之，太祖亦從之。

translations.literal: Yan's nephew Chongxun lived in Chen commandery; Jun sought official fields and a mansion to bestow on him, and the Taizu also assented.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's nephew Chongxun lived in Chen prefecture; Wang Jun asked that official fields and a residence be granted him, and Guo Wei agreed.

sentences.zh: 三年春，修利河堤，大興土功，峻受詔檢校。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, the benefit river dikes were repaired and earthworks were raised on a great scale; Jun received orders to inspect the work.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the third year, work began on repairing the Benefit River dikes on a large scale; Wang Jun was ordered to supervise it.

sentences.zh: 既而世宗自澶州入覲，峻素憚世宗之聰明英果，聞其赴闕，即自河次歸朝。

translations.literal: Before long Shizong came from Cangzhou to audience; Jun had always feared Shizong's intelligence and resolution; hearing he was coming to court, he returned from the river works at once.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Shizong came from Cangzhou to audience. Wang Jun had always been wary of his intelligence and force of character; hearing he was on his way to the capital, Wang Jun left the river project and hurried back.

sentences.zh: 居無何，邀求兼領青州，太祖不得已而授之。

translations.literal: After little time he pressed to hold Qing Prefecture concurrently; the Taizu, unable to refuse, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he demanded concurrent appointment as military governor of Qingzhou; Guo Wei, unable to refuse, granted it.

sentences.zh: 既受命，求暫赴任，奏借左藏綾絹萬匹，從之。

translations.literal: Once he had received the appointment he asked leave to go briefly to his post and memorialized to borrow ten thousand bolts of silk from the left treasury; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: After accepting the post he asked permission to take up office for a time and memorialized to borrow ten thousand bolts of silk from the left treasury; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，戶部侍郎趙上交權知貢舉，上交嘗詣峻，峻言及一童子，上交不達其旨，榜出之日，童子不第，峻銜之。

translations.literal: That year Vice Minister of Revenue Zhao Shangjiao held acting charge of the civil examinations; Shangjiao had once called on Jun, and Jun spoke of a certain youth; Shangjiao did not grasp his intent; when the list was published the youth failed; Jun bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhao Shangjiao, vice minister of revenue, acted as chief examiner. He had once visited Wang Jun, who mentioned a certain young candidate; Shangjiao did not catch his meaning. When the results were posted the youth failed, and Wang Jun took offense.

sentences.zh: 及貢院申中書門下，取日過堂，峻知印，判定過日。

translations.literal: When the examination office reported to the Secretariat and Chancellery to set a day for the court audience, Jun affixed the seal and fixed the day for passage.
translations.idiomatic: When the examination office reported to the Secretariat to schedule the palace audience, Wang Jun applied the seal and set the date.

sentences.zh: 及上交引新及第人至中書，峻在政事堂厲聲曰：「今歲選士不公，當須覆試。

translations.literal: When Shangjiao led the new graduates to the Secretariat, Jun in the Hall of Administration said in a loud voice, "This year's selection of scholars was unjust and must be re-examined."
translations.idiomatic: When Shangjiao brought the new jinshi to the Secretariat, Wang Jun shouted in the Hall of Administration, "This year's examination was unfair and must be retested."

sentences.zh: 」諸相曰：「但緣已行指揮行過，臨事不欲改移，況未敕下，覆試非晚。

translations.literal: The chief ministers said, "But an order has already been issued and carried out; we do not wish to change matters on the spot; moreover the edict has not yet been promulgated—retesting is not too late."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers said, "The directive has already gone out; we do not want to alter things at the last moment. Besides, the edict has not yet been promulgated—a retest can wait."

sentences.zh: 」峻愈怒，詬責上交，聲聞於外。

translations.literal: Jun grew still angrier, reviled Shangjiao, and the sound was heard outside.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun grew angrier still, berated Shangjiao, and his voice carried outside the hall.

sentences.zh: 少頃，竟令引過。

translations.literal: Before long he nevertheless ordered them led through.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he still ordered the graduates presented.

sentences.zh: 及罷，上交詣本廳謝峻，峻又延之飲酌從容。

translations.literal: When it was over, Shangjiao went to his bureau to apologize to Jun, and Jun again received him for drink in an easy manner.
translations.idiomatic: When the audience ended, Shangjiao went to Wang Jun's office to apologize, and Wang Jun received him again for a relaxed drink.

sentences.zh: 翌日，峻奏上交知舉不公，請致之於法，太祖頷之而已。

translations.literal: The next day Jun memorialized that Shangjiao's conduct of the examination was unjust and asked that he be punished by law; the Taizu only nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wang Jun memorialized that Shangjiao had run the examination unfairly and asked that he be punished; Guo Wei only nodded.

sentences.zh: 又奏請以顏愆、陳觀代範質、李穀為相。

translations.literal: He also memorialized asking that Yan Qian and Chen Guan replace Fan Zhi and Li Gu as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Yan Qian and Chen Guan replace Fan Zhi and Li Gu as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「進退宰輔，未可倉卒，待徐思之。

translations.literal: The Taizu said, "Advancing and dismissing chief ministers cannot be done in haste; wait and consider it slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei said, "Promoting and dismissing chief ministers cannot be rushed; let us think on it awhile."

sentences.zh: 」峻論列其事，奏對不遜。

translations.literal: Jun argued the matter at length in memorial and audience without deference.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun argued the point at length in audience, his replies lacking all deference.

sentences.zh: 太祖未食，日將亭午，諍之不已。

translations.literal: The Taizu had not eaten; the sun was nearing noon, and Jun remonstrated without end.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei had not yet eaten; the sun was nearly at noon, and Wang Jun would not stop arguing.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「節假之內，未欲便行，已俟假開，即依所奏。

translations.literal: The Taizu said, "Within the holiday period I do not wish to act at once; wait until the holiday ends and I will follow your memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei said, "During the holiday I do not wish to act hastily. When the holiday ends I will do as you ask."

sentences.zh: 」峻退至中書。

translations.literal: Jun withdrew to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun withdrew to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是月，吏部選人過門下，峻當其事，頗疑選部不公，其擬官選人落下者三十餘人。

translations.literal: That month, candidates of the Ministry of Personnel passed the Gate Department; Jun was in charge of the matter, strongly suspected the selection bureau of injustice, and struck more than thirty proposed appointees from the list.
translations.idiomatic: That month civil-service candidates passed review at the Gate Department under Wang Jun's authority. He suspected the selection bureau of bias and struck more than thirty proposed appointees from the list.

sentences.zh: 次日寒食時節，臣僚各歸私第。

translations.literal: The next day was the Cold Food Festival; the officials each returned to private residences.
translations.idiomatic: The next day was Cold Food; the officials went home.

sentences.zh: 午時，宣召宰臣、樞密使，及入，幽峻於別所。

translations.literal: At noon the emperor summoned the chief ministers and commissioner of military affairs; when they entered, Jun was confined in a separate place.
translations.idiomatic: At noon Guo Wei summoned the chief ministers and the military-affairs commissioner. When they arrived, Wang Jun was held apart.

sentences.zh: 太祖見馮道已下，泣曰：「峻淩朕頗甚，無禮太過，擬欲盡去左右臣僚，翦朕羽翼。

translations.literal: The Taizu, seeing Feng Dao and the rest, wept and said, "Jun has bullied Us greatly, his lack of courtesy excessive; he intends to remove all Our close ministers and cut off Our wings."
translations.idiomatic: Facing Feng Dao and the others, Guo Wei wept and said, "Wang Jun has bullied me terribly, with insolence beyond bearing. He means to drive away every minister at my side and cut off my wings."

sentences.zh: 朕兒在外，專意阻隔，暫令到闕，即懷怨望。

translations.literal: My son is outside; he deliberately blocks him; when I briefly let him reach court he already harbors resentment.
translations.idiomatic: My son is kept away outside the capital; Wang Jun deliberately blocks him. When I briefly let him come to court he is already full of grievance.

sentences.zh: 豈有既總樞機，又兼宰相，堅求重鎮，尋亦授之，任其襟懷，尚未厭足，如此無君，誰能甘忍！

translations.literal: How can one who already holds the Bureau of Military Affairs, who is also chief minister, who pressed for a great frontier post and was soon granted it, and whose desires are still not satisfied—how can such a man without regard for his lord be endured!"
translations.idiomatic: He already commands the Bureau of Military Affairs, is also chief minister, demanded a major frontier post and got it, and still his appetite is not sated. Who could bear such disloyalty!

sentences.zh: 」即召翰林學士徐臺符等草制。

translations.literal: He at once summoned Hanlin academician Xu Taifu and others to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately summoned Hanlin academician Xu Taifu and others to draft the demotion edict.

sentences.zh: 其日，退朝宣制，貶授商州司馬，差供奉官蔣光遠援送赴商州。

translations.literal: That day, after court the edict was proclaimed: he was demoted to military adjutant of Shang Prefecture, and palace supply officer Jiang Guangyuan was sent to escort him to Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That day, after court, the edict was read: Wang Jun was demoted to military adjutant of Shangzhou, and palace supply officer Jiang Guangyuan was sent to escort him thither.

sentences.zh: 未幾，死於貶所，時廣順三年三月也。

translations.literal: Before long he died at his place of exile, in the third month of the third year of Guangshun.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in exile, in the third month of Guangshun's third year.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：峻至商州，得腹疾，帝猶湣之，命其妻往視之，未幾而卒。）〉

translations.literal: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: When Jun reached Shang Prefecture he developed abdominal illness; the emperor still pitied him and ordered his wife to go see him; before long he died.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: When Wang Jun reached Shangzhou he fell ill with abdominal disease. The emperor still pitied him and sent his wife to visit him; before long he died.)〉

sentences.zh: 初，峻降制除青州，有司制造旌節，以備迎授。

translations.literal: At first, when the demotion edict removed Jun to Qing Prefecture, the relevant offices manufactured banners of command to prepare for his investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the edict demoting Wang Jun assigned him to Qingzhou, the proper offices had begun making banners of command for his installation.

sentences.zh: 前一夕，其旄有聲甚異，聞者駭之。

translations.literal: On the eve before, his banner staff made a very strange sound, and those who heard were alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: On the night before, his command banners gave off a very strange noise, and those who heard it were frightened.

sentences.zh: 主者曰：「昔安重誨授河中節，亦有此異焉。

translations.literal: The keeper said, "In the past when An Chonghui received the Bingzhong commission there was also this anomaly."
translations.idiomatic: The custodian said, "When An Chonghui received the Bingzhong commission there was this same omen."

sentences.zh: 」又所居堂陛，忽然隱起如堆。

translations.literal: Moreover the hall steps of his residence suddenly swelled up as if heaped.
translations.idiomatic: The steps of his hall also suddenly bulged upward like a mound.

sentences.zh: 又夢被官府追攝入司簿院，既寤，心惡之，以是尤加狂躁。

translations.literal: He also dreamed he was seized by the authorities and taken into the Bureau of Registers; when he awoke his heart hated it, and for this he grew still more frantic.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed officials seized him and dragged him into the Bureau of Registers. When he woke he was filled with dread and grew all the more frantic.

sentences.zh: 峻才疏位重，輕躁寡謀，聽人穿鼻，既國權在手，而射利者曲為指畫，乃啖餌虎臣，離間親舊，加以善則稱己，無禮於君，欲求無罪，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Jun's talent was slight and his position heavy; he was light, rash, and short on counsel, letting others lead him by the nose; once state power was in his hands, those who sought profit twisted plans for him, baiting fierce ministers and estranging kin and old friends; moreover he claimed credit for what was good and was without courtesy toward his lord—how could he hope to be without guilt!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's talent did not match his rank. Impulsive and scheming little, he let others lead him about. Once he held state power, profiteers bent plans to their ends, baiting fierce ministers and driving wedges between the emperor and his old companions. He took credit for every good turn and showed his sovereign no courtesy. How could he expect to escape guilt!

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《五代史闕文》：廣順初，河東劉崇引契丹攻晉州。

translations.literal: (《五代史闕文》: Early in Guangshun, Liu Chong of Hedong brought the Khitan to attack Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: (《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Early in Guangshun, Liu Chong of Hedong brought Khitan forces against Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣王峻率師赴援，峻頓兵於陜。

translations.literal: Wang Jun was sent with an army in relief; Jun halted his troops at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was dispatched to relieve the city and camped his army at Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 周祖親征，遣使諭之。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder campaigned in person and sent an envoy to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei took the field in person and sent an envoy to instruct him.

sentences.zh: 峻見使受宣訖，謂使曰：「與某馳還，附奏陛下，言晉州城堅，未易可破，劉崇兵鋒方銳，不可與力爭，所以駐兵者，待其氣衰耳，非臣怯也。

translations.literal: When Jun saw the envoy and received the imperial message, he told the envoy, "Ride back with me and report to His Majesty: Jin Prefecture's walls are strong and not easily taken; Liu Chong's troops are at the height of their edge and cannot be met in force; the reason I halt the army is to wait until their spirit declines—it is not that your servant is cowardly.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun received the envoy and heard the imperial message, he told him, "Ride back with me and report to His Majesty: Jinzhou's walls are strong and will not fall easily; Liu Chong's troops are at their sharpest and cannot be met head-on. I am holding my army here only until their ardor fades—it is not cowardice."

sentences.zh: 陛下新即位，不宜輕舉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly ascended; you should not act lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only just taken the throne; you should not take risks lightly.

sentences.zh: 今朝中受聖知者，惟李蒨、範質而已，陛下若車駕出汜水，則慕容彥超以賊軍入汴，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Those in court today who enjoy the sage's trust are only Li Qian and Fan Zhi; if Your Majesty's carriage goes out beyond Sishui, Murong Yanchao will lead rebel troops into Bian and the great enterprise will be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Of those at court who enjoy your full trust today, only Li Qian and Fan Zhi remain. If Your Majesty's carriage goes beyond Sishui, Murong Yanchao will lead rebel troops into Bian—the whole enterprise will be lost."

sentences.zh: 」使還具奏，周祖自以手提其耳曰：「幾敗吾事。」）〉

translations.literal: The envoy returned and reported in full; the Zhou founder took his own ear in hand and said, "I nearly ruined my affair." )〉
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy returned and reported everything, Guo Wei seized his own ear and said, "I nearly ruined everything.")〉

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超，

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao,
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （案：此下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: There is missing text below.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Editorial note: Text is missing below.)〉

sentences.zh: 為兗州節度使，彥超即漢高祖之同產弟也。

translations.literal: served as military governor of Yan Prefecture; Yanchao was the uterine younger brother of the Han founder.
translations.idiomatic: was military governor of Yanzhou; Yanchao was the Han founder's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 嘗冒姓閻氏，體黑麻面，故謂之閻昆侖。

translations.literal: He had once taken the surname Yan; his body was black and his face pockmarked, so he was called Yan Kunlun.
translations.idiomatic: He had once borne the surname Yan; dark-skinned and pockmarked, he was nicknamed "Yan Kunlun."

sentences.zh: 彥超鎮兗州，漢隱帝欲殺周太祖，召彥超，方食，釋匕箸而就道。

translations.literal: When Yanchao held Yan Prefecture, the Hidden Emperor of Han wished to kill the Zhou founder and summoned Yanchao; he was at his meal and set down spoon and chopsticks to take the road.
translations.idiomatic: While Yanchao governed Yanzhou, Emperor Yin of Later Han plotted to kill Guo Wei and summoned him. Yanchao was in the middle of a meal but laid down his utensils and set out at once.

sentences.zh: 周兵犯京師，隱帝出勞軍，太后使彥超衛帝，彥超曰：「北兵何能為，當於陣上唱坐使歸營。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops threatened the capital, the Hidden Emperor went out to encourage the army; the empress dowager ordered Yanchao to guard the emperor; Yanchao said, "What can the northern soldiers do? I shall stand on the line and sing for them to sit down and return to camp."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou forces threatened the capital, the Hidden Emperor went out to review the troops. The empress dowager ordered Yanchao to protect him. Yanchao said, "What can those northern soldiers do? I'll stand on the battlefield and sing them back to camp."

sentences.zh: 」彥超敗，奔兗，隱帝遇弒。

translations.literal: Yanchao was defeated and fled to Yan; the Hidden Emperor met assassination.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao was beaten and fled to Yanzhou; the Hidden Emperor was murdered.

sentences.zh: 周太祖時，彥超進呈鄆州節度使高行周來書，其書意即行周毀讟太祖結連彥超之意，帝覽之，笑曰：「此必是彥超之詐也。

translations.literal: In the time of the Zhou founder, Yanchao presented a letter said to come from Yanzhou military governor Gao Xingzhou; the letter's intent was that Xingzhou slandered the founder and was in league with Yanchao; the emperor read it and laughed, "This must be Yanchao's fraud."
translations.idiomatic: During Guo Wei's reign, Yanchao submitted a letter purportedly from Yanzhou governor Gao Xingzhou, implying that Xingzhou had slandered Guo Wei and was conspiring with Yanchao. Guo Wei read it and laughed, "This must be Yanchao's trick."

sentences.zh: 」試令驗之，果然。

translations.literal: When he ordered it verified, it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: An investigation proved it at once.

sentences.zh: 其鄆州印元有缺，文不相接，其為印即無缺處，帝尋令賫書示諭行周，行周上表謝恩。

translations.literal: The Yan Prefecture seal originally had a gap so the text did not join; the forged seal had no gap; the emperor soon sent the letter to show and instruct Xingzhou, and Xingzhou submitted a memorial thanking for grace.
translations.idiomatic: The genuine Yanzhou seal had a flaw where the characters did not meet; the forged seal had no such gap. Guo Wei soon sent the letter to Gao Xingzhou to show him what had been done, and Xingzhou submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 先是，填星初至角、亢，占者曰：角，鄭分，兗州屬焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Piled Star first reached Horn and Neck, the diviners said, "Horn is the allotment of Zheng; Yan Prefecture belongs to it."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Piled Star entered the Horn and Neck lodges, diviners said, "Horn is Zheng's celestial allotment, and Yanzhou falls within it."

sentences.zh: 彥超即率軍府賓佐，步出州西門三十里致祭，迎於開元寺，塑像以事之，謂之「菩薩」，日至祈禱，又令民家豎黃幡以禳之。

translations.literal: Yanchao at once led the military staff and guests, walked out the west gate of the prefecture thirty li to offer sacrifice, received it at Kaiyuan Temple, set up an image to serve it, calling it "Bodhisattva," prayed day by day, and also ordered households to raise yellow banners to avert it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao led his staff out the west gate thirty li to make offerings, welcomed the omen at Kaiyuan Temple, and set up an image to worship it as the "Bodhisattva." He prayed daily and ordered households to raise yellow banners to ward off ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，彥超方在土星院燃香，急乃馳去。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Yanchao was still burning incense at the Saturn Courtyard and fled in haste.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Yanchao was still burning incense at the Saturn Courtyard and fled in panic.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：慕容彥超素有鉤距。

translations.literal: (《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Murong Yanchao had always been full of schemes.
translations.idiomatic: (《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Murong Yanchao was always full of stratagems.

sentences.zh: 兗州有盜者，詐為大官從人，跨驢於衢中，市羅十餘匹，價值既定，引物主詣一宅門，以驢付之，曰：「此本宅使，汝且在此，吾為汝上白於主以請值。

translations.literal: In Yan Prefecture there was a thief who pretended to be an attendant of a great official, riding a donkey in the market street, buying more than ten bolts of silk; once the price was set he led the owner to a mansion gate, handed him the donkey, and said, "This is our master's residence; wait here while I go up and report to the master to request payment."
translations.idiomatic: At Yanzhou a thief posed as a great official's attendant, riding a donkey through the streets to buy more than ten bolts of silk. When the price was agreed he led the seller to a mansion gate, handed him the donkey, and said, "This is our master's house. Wait here while I report upstairs and get your payment."

sentences.zh: 」物主許之。

translations.literal: The owner agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The seller agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而聲跡悄然，物主怒其不出，叩門呼之，則空宅也。

translations.literal: Before long all sound and trace fell silent; the owner, angry that he did not come out, knocked and called at the gate, but it was an empty house.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all went quiet. Angry that no one appeared, the seller knocked and shouted at the gate, only to find an empty house.

sentences.zh: 於是連叫「賊」，巡司至，疑其詐，兼以驢收之詣府。

translations.literal: He then cried "Thief!" repeatedly; the patrol arrived, suspected his fraud, and also took the donkey with him to the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: He began shouting "Thief!" The patrol came, suspected him of fraud, and took the donkey to the prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 彥超憫之，且曰：「勿憂，吾為汝擒此賊。

translations.literal: Yanchao pitied him and said, "Do not worry; I will capture this thief for you."
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao took pity on him and said, "Do not worry; I will catch this thief for you."

sentences.zh: 」乃留物主府中，復戒廄卒高系其驢，通宵不與水草，然後密召親信者，牽於通衢中放之，且曰：「此盜者之驢耳，自昨日不與水草，其饑渴者甚矣，放之必奔歸家，但可躡蹤而觀之，盜無不獲也。

translations.literal: He kept the owner at the office, again warned the stable hands to tie the donkey high and give it no fodder or water all night, then secretly summoned a trusted man, led it out into the main street and released it, saying, "This is the thief's donkey; since yesterday it has had no fodder or water and is very hungry and thirsty; if released it will surely run home; you need only follow its tracks and watch; thieves are never not caught."
translations.idiomatic: He kept the seller at his headquarters, ordered the stable hands to tie the donkey high and withhold fodder and water all night, then secretly told a trusted man to lead it into the main street and release it, saying, "This is the thief's donkey. Without food or water since yesterday it must be desperate; release it and it will run home. Follow its tracks and you cannot fail to catch the thief."

sentences.zh: 」親信者如其言隨之，其驢果入一小巷，轉數曲，忽有兒戲於門側，視其驢，連呼曰：「驢歸，驢歸。

translations.literal: The trusted man followed as he said; the donkey indeed entered a small lane, turned several bends, and suddenly a child played beside a gate, saw its donkey, and cried again and again, "The donkey is back, the donkey is back."
translations.idiomatic: The man did as told. The donkey entered a small lane, wound through several turns, and a child playing by a gate saw it and cried, "The donkey's back! The donkey's back!"

sentences.zh: 」盜者聞之，欣然出視，遂擒之。

translations.literal: The thief heard it, came out gladly to look, and was seized.
translations.idiomatic: The thief heard him, came out gladly to look, and was captured.

sentences.zh: 高祖登極，改乾祐為廣順。

translations.literal: When the founder ascended the throne he changed Qianyou to Guangshun.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei took the throne he changed the reign title from Qianyou to Guangshun.

sentences.zh: 是年，兗州慕容彥超反。

translations.literal: That year Murong Yanchao rebelled at Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year Murong Yanchao rebelled at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖親征，城將破，忽夜夢一人，狀貌甚偉異，被王者之服，謂高祖曰：「陛下明日當得城。

translations.literal: The founder campaigned in person; as the city was about to fall, he suddenly dreamed of a man of very strange appearance, wearing kingly robes, who told the founder, "Tomorrow Your Majesty will take the city."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei campaigned in person. As the city was about to fall he dreamed of a man of striking appearance in kingly robes who said, "Tomorrow Your Majesty will take the city."

sentences.zh: 」及覺，天猶未曉。

translations.literal: When he awoke, dawn had not yet broken.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke, dawn had not yet broken.

sentences.zh: 高祖私謂征兆如此，可不預備乎！

translations.literal: The founder said privately, "With an omen like this, how can I not prepare!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei said to himself, "With an omen like this, how can I fail to prepare!"

sentences.zh: 於是躬督將士，戮力急攻，至午而城陷。

translations.literal: He therefore personally directed the generals and soldiers, striving with all their strength in urgent attack, and by noon the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: He personally directed his officers in a furious assault, and by noon the city fell.

sentences.zh: 車駕將入，有司請由生方鳴鞘而進，遂取別巷，轉數曲，見一處門墻甚高大，問之，雲夫子廟。

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to enter, the relevant offices asked that it enter by the life-direction with whip sounding; he therefore took a side lane, turned several bends, and saw a gate and wall very tall and great; on asking, they said it was the temple of the Master.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial carriage was about to enter, officials asked that it approach from the auspicious direction with the whip sounded. He took a side lane instead, wound through several turns, and came upon a gate and wall of great height. Inquiring, he learned it was the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 高祖意豁然，謂近臣曰：「寡人所夢，得非夫子乎？

translations.literal: The founder's mind suddenly cleared and he told his close ministers, "Could the one in my dream be the Master?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei's mind cleared at once. He told his close ministers, "Could the figure in my dream have been Confucius?"

sentences.zh: 不然，何取路於此也。

translations.literal: If not, why take a road that comes here?"
translations.idiomatic: If not, why should our route have brought us here?"

sentences.zh: 」因下馬觀之，方升堂，睹其聖像，一如夢中所見者，於是大喜，叩首再拜。

translations.literal: He therefore dismounted to view it; as he was ascending the hall he saw the sage's image, exactly like the one in his dream; he was greatly pleased and bowed his head twice.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted to look. As he ascended the hall he saw the sage's image, exactly as in his dream. Overjoyed, he bowed twice.

sentences.zh: 近臣或諫，以為天子不合拜異世陪臣。

translations.literal: Close ministers some remonstrated, holding that the Son of Heaven should not bow to a minister of another age.
translations.idiomatic: Some close ministers objected that the Son of Heaven ought not bow to a minister of another age.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「夫子聖人也，百王取則，而又夢告寡人，得非夫子幽贊所及耶？

translations.literal: The founder said, "The Master is a sage; the hundred kings take him as model; moreover he told me in a dream—could it not be that the Master secretly aided from the unseen?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei said, "Confucius is a sage whom a hundred kings take as their model. He also warned me in a dream. Could this not be his hidden blessing?"

sentences.zh: 安得不拜！

translations.literal: How could I not bow!"
translations.idiomatic: How could I not bow!"

sentences.zh: 」仍以廟側數十家為灑掃戶，命孔氏襲文宣王者長為本縣。

translations.literal: He also made several tens of households beside the temple sweeping households and ordered the Kong clan heir to the Duke of Wenxuan to be elder of the county.
translations.idiomatic: He made several dozen households beside the temple temple sweepers and appointed the Kong clan heir to the title Duke of Wenxuan as elder of the county.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超之被圍也，乘城而望，見高祖親臨矢石，其勢不可當，退而憂之，因勉其麾下曰：「汝等宜為吾盡命，吾庫中金銀如山積，若全此城，吾盡以為賜，汝等勿患富貴。

translations.literal: When Murong Yanchao was besieged, he climbed the wall to look and saw the founder personally under arrows and stones; the momentum could not be withstood; he withdrew and worried, then urged his subordinates, "You should give your lives for me; the gold and silver in my treasury are piled like mountains; if this city is preserved I will give it all as reward; you need not worry about wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: While Murong Yanchao was under siege he climbed the wall and saw Guo Wei himself in the hail of arrows and stones. The assault was irresistible. He withdrew in alarm and urged his men, "Fight for me with all you have. Gold and silver in my treasury are heaped like mountains. Save this city and I will give it all to you; you need not fear for wealth or rank."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，有卒私言曰：「我知侍中銀皆鐵胎，得之何用？

translations.literal: Before long a soldier said privately, "I know the attendant's silver is all iron core—what use is getting it?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon a soldier whispered, "I know the commander's silver is all iron at the core. What's the use of that?"

sentences.zh: 」於是諸軍聞之，稍稍解體，未幾城陷。

translations.literal: When the armies heard this they gradually fell apart, and before long the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops heard this they slowly lost heart, and before long the city fell.

sentences.zh: 及高祖之入也，有司閱其庫藏，其間銀鐵胎者果十有七八。

translations.literal: When the founder entered, the relevant offices examined his treasury stores; among them iron-core silver indeed made up seven or eight tenths.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei entered, officials inspected the treasury. Seven or eight tenths of the silver proved to be iron at the core.

sentences.zh: 初，彥超常令人開質庫，有以鐵胎銀質錢者，經年後，庫吏始覺，遂言之於彥超。

translations.literal: At first Yanchao often had men open pawnshops; some pawned iron-core silver for cash; after more than a year the shop clerks first noticed it and reported to Yanchao.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao often had pawnshops opened in his domain. Some customers pawned iron-core silver. More than a year passed before the clerks noticed and reported it to him.

sentences.zh: 初甚怒，頃之謂吏曰：「此易致耳，汝宜偽竇刂庫墻，凡金銀器用暨縑帛等，速皆藏匿，仍亂撤其餘以為賊踐，然後申明，吾當擒此輩矣。

translations.literal: At first he was very angry; before long he told the clerk, "This is easy to achieve; you should feign a break in the pawnshop wall; quickly hide all gold and silver vessels and silks; still scatter the rest as if trampled by thieves, then report it; I will seize this lot."
translations.idiomatic: At first he was furious; then he told the clerk, "This is easy to fix. Pretend thieves broke through the pawnshop wall. Hide all gold and silver goods and silks at once, scatter the rest as if thieves trampled them, then report the burglary. I will catch these people."

sentences.zh: 」庫吏如其教，於是彥超下令曰：「吾為使長典百姓，而又不謹，遭賊竇刂去，其過深矣。

translations.literal: The shop clerk followed his instruction; Yanchao then issued an order, "I am commissioner charged with the common people, yet I was not careful and suffered thieves breaking in; the fault is deep."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk did as instructed. Yanchao then proclaimed, "As commissioner I am charged with the people, yet I was careless and thieves broke in. The fault is grave."

sentences.zh: 今恐百姓疑彥超隱其物，宜令三日內各投狀，明言質物色，自當陪償之，不爾者有過。

translations.literal: Now I fear the people suspect Yanchao of hiding their goods; they should within three days each submit a statement clearly stating the pawned goods by kind; I will compensate them myself; otherwise there is fault."
translations.idiomatic: I fear the people may think I am hiding their goods. Within three days each of you must submit a statement describing your pawned items in detail. I will compensate you myself. Anyone who does not will be at fault."

sentences.zh: 」百姓以為然，於是投狀相繼，翌日鐵胎銀主果出。

translations.literal: The people thought it so, and statements were submitted in succession; the next day the owners of iron-core silver indeed came forward.
translations.idiomatic: The people believed him, and statements poured in. The next day the owners of iron-core silver appeared.

sentences.zh: 於是擒之，置之深屋中，使教部曲輩晝夜造，用廣府庫，此銀是也。）〉

translations.literal: They were then seized and placed in a deep room, made to teach their followers to work day and night to manufacture it, to fill the prefectural treasury; this was that silver.)〉
translations.idiomatic: They were seized, shut in a deep chamber, and made to teach their gangs to forge day and night to fill the prefectural treasury. That was the silver in question.)〉

sentences.zh: 閻宏魯者，後唐邢州節度使寶之子也。

translations.literal: Yan Honglu was the son of Bao, military governor of Xing Prefecture in Later Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Honglu was the son of Yan Bao, military governor of Xingzhou under Later Tang.

sentences.zh: 寶，《唐書》有傳。

translations.literal: Bao has a biography in the Tang History.
translations.idiomatic: Bao has a biography in the Tang History.

sentences.zh: 宏魯事唐明宗、晉高祖，累歷事任。

translations.literal: Honglu served Emperor Mingzong of Tang and Emperor Gaozu of Jin, accumulating offices through successive appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Honglu served Emperor Mingzong of Tang and Emperor Gaozu of Later Jin, rising through a series of posts.

sentences.zh: 家本魯中，洎告疾歸裏，慕容彥超初臨，禮待極厚。

translations.literal: His family was originally from central Lu; when he reported illness and returned home, Murong Yanchao on first arrival treated him with the utmost courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: His family came from the Lu region. When he went home on sick leave, Murong Yanchao on first taking Yanzhou treated him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 及謀大逆，以宏魯子希俊為鎮寧軍節度副使，在世宗幕下而惡之。

translations.literal: When he plotted great treason he made Honglu's son Xijun deputy military commissioner of Zhenning Army; Xijun was under Shizong's command and Yanchao hated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanchao plotted rebellion he made Honglu's son Xijun deputy military commissioner of Zhenning, stationed on Shizong's staff, whom Yanchao hated.

sentences.zh: 聞朝廷出兵堤防，即責宏魯曰：「爾教兒捍我於朝，將覆吾族耶！

translations.literal: Hearing the court had sent troops on guard, he at once reproached Honglu, "You taught your son to block me at court—will you overthrow my clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the court was sending troops against him, he rebuked Honglu at once: "You taught your son to oppose me at court. Do you mean to destroy my whole clan!"

sentences.zh: 」故罹其禍。

translations.literal: Therefore he suffered this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: For this he suffered death.

sentences.zh: 崔周度者，父光表，舉進士甲科，盧質節制橫海，辟為支使。

translations.literal: Cui Zhoudu—his father Guangbiao passed the jinshi in the first class; Lu Zhi governed Henghai and recruited him as branch commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhoudu's father Guangbiao passed the jinshi examination in the top class. When Lu Zhi governed Henghai he recruited him as branch commissioner.

sentences.zh: 周度有文學，起家長蘆令，登朝歷監察御史、右補闕，以家在齊州，欲謀葬事，懇求外任，除泰寧軍節度判官。

translations.literal: Zhoudu had literary talent, rose from magistrate of Changlu, entered court and passed through investigating censor and right remonstrator; because his family was in Qi Prefecture and he wished to arrange burial affairs, he earnestly sought an outer post and was made military commissioner's judge of Taining Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhoudu was a man of letters, beginning as magistrate of Changlu and entering court as investigating censor and right remonstrator. Wishing to arrange his family's burial in Qi Prefecture, he begged for an outside post and was made judge on the staff of the Taining military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 而性剛烈，又以嘗為諫官，睹兇帥之不法，不忍坐視其弊，因極言以諫彥超，故及斯禍。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was stern and fierce, and because he had once been a remonstrator, seeing the fierce governor's lawlessness he could not bear to sit and watch the harm, and therefore spoke to the utmost in remonstrance to Yanchao; for this he met this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was stern, and having once served as a remonstrator he could not sit by while the rebel governor broke the law. He remonstrated with Yanchao to the utmost and for that met this fate.

sentences.zh: 太祖平兗州，詔曰：「閻宏魯、崔周度，死義之臣，禮加二等，所以滲漏澤而賁黃泉也。

translations.literal: When the founder pacified Yan Prefecture, an edict said, "Yan Honglu and Cui Zhoudu were ministers who died for righteousness; ritual is raised two grades, thereby letting favor seep down and adorn the yellow springs."
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei pacified Yanzhou, an edict said, "Yan Honglu and Cui Zhoudu were ministers who died for righteousness. Their rites are raised two grades, so that favor may seep down to adorn the yellow springs."

sentences.zh: 爾等貞節昭彰，正容肅厲，以從順為己任，以立義作身謀，履此禍機，並罹冤橫，宜伸贈典，以慰貞魂。

translations.literal: Your loyal integrity shines clear, your upright bearing stern and severe; you took compliance as your charge and establishing righteousness as your life's plan; you trod this pit of calamity and together met wrongful death; posthumous honors should be extended to comfort loyal souls."
translations.idiomatic: Your steadfast integrity shines forth, your bearing upright and stern. You took obedience as your duty and righteousness as your life's plan. You fell into this calamity and together met wrongful death. Posthumous honors should be granted to comfort your loyal souls."

sentences.zh: 宏魯可贈左驍衛大將軍，周度可贈秘書少監。」

translations.literal: Honglu may be posthumously granted Left Valiant Cavalry Grand General; Zhoudu may be posthumously granted Vice Director of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Honglu is posthumously granted Left Valiant Cavalry Grand General; Zhoudu is posthumously granted Vice Director of the Secretariat."
